findings.summary: The estimate of the athena-bin key count is wrong; do not hard-code it in the test.
findings.evidence: A grep of .github/workflows/ci.yml for `athena-bin` finds 9 key lines (175, 231, 278, 334, 387, 445, 583, 659, 701), not 11. policy.rs:965-970 says there are six restore steps and three save steps. Fix: Do not hard-code a key count in build_inputs.rs. If a count is wanted, assert at least one key, or derive the count the way policy.rs does. Correct the estimate in the plan.
findings.location: Plan, Demonstrations, Criterion 2 ("11 athena-bin key lines ... 6 restore and 5 save")

findings.summary: The help text and the drain.rs doc comment will name the old five-entry list after the widening.
findings.evidence: After the widening, the user-facing help text and the drain.rs module doc (drain.rs:109) still list only crates/, xtask/, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock and setup.sh. The plan names them as a follow-up only. Fix: Keep them as a follow-up, but name them explicitly in the CHANGELOG entry and in D154 as now-stale text, so a newcomer reading the help text is not misled. Optionally ask for main.rs to be added as a deliverable.
findings.location: Plan, Decision 6 and Open questions (main.rs:250 help text, drain.rs:109 comment)

findings.summary: The ci.yml half of the new test repeats an existing check in policy.rs.
findings.evidence: policy.rs:899-934 `check_athena_bin_keys` already checks that every athena-bin key covers the compiled-in set. The ci.yml half of the new test repeats it. Only the BUILD_PATHS half is new. Fix: In D154, say that the ci.yml check repeats policy.rs on purpose and that the BUILD_PATHS check is the new part. Keep the scan rules the same, as planned.
findings.location: Plan, Decision 1 / Open questions (overlap with xtask/tests/policy.rs)

findings.summary: Matching every `athena-bin-` line would break on a future restore-keys line.
findings.evidence: Today every `athena-bin-` line in ci.yml is a `key:` line with hashFiles. A future `restore-keys: athena-bin-...` prefix line would fail this rule, even though such a line has no hashFiles by design. Fix: Match `key: athena-bin-` the way policy.rs:907 does, or exempt `restore-keys` lines.
findings.location: Plan, Step 3 (lines containing `athena-bin-` with no hashFiles are reported)

summary: The plan fits the request and the reading. It adds one file-read-only integration test that finds the compiled-in inputs using the same rules as xtask/tests/policy.rs `compiled_in_files` (policy.rs:842-882, read). It checks those inputs against every athena-bin hashFiles key in ci.yml and against BUILD_PATHS. To make that possible it adds a small `path_in` helper that touches_build uses, so the test checks the real matching rule. I confirmed the gap the plan names is real. `BUILTIN_CONFIG = include_str!("../../../athena.toml")` is at athena-gate/src/lib.rs:33, before that file's first #[cfg(test)] at line 387. `SYSTEM_FACTS` is at athena-context/src/briefs.rs:1230, before line 1933. BUILD_PATHS (status.rs:20) covers neither file. The defaults.toml includes in athena-data (config.rs:776, defaults.rs:89) come after the #[cfg(test)] lines at 771 and 85, so leaving defaults.toml out of BUILD_PATHS is right. The existing tests at cli tests/drain.rs:1421 and 1499 only assert the old paths as "yes" and docs/records as "no", and they do not match on the message text, so widening the list should not break them. The plan rightly leaves that to a workspace test run. Each fixture asserts on the error text, the fixtures use the production `path_in` as the seam, and the test calls no external service. Only minor findings remain.
